newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission takes action against OCT rice imports.
newsitem.headline: Commission takes action against OCT rice imports.

text.p: The European Union has imposed safeguard measures against imports of rice from its overseas countries and territories (OCT), the European Commission said on Wednesday.

The move followed a complaint from Italy that a 48 percent rise in imports to 284,000 tonnes by end-November 1996, compared with the year-ago period, endangered EU indica rice producers. Imports amounted to only 58,000 tonnes in 1992.
"In these circumstances the Commission decided to urgently implement the first phase of the safeguard procedure -- to inform member states and convoke the advisory committee," it said in a statement.
It will apply safeguard measures in a second phase.

In 1991 the EU agreed that rice produced in African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) member countries of the Lome convention could enjoy the free access granted the OCT countries after a small amount of processing.
Increasing amounts of rice from the ACP states of Guyana and Surinam were processed mainly in the Dutch Antilles before being exported to the EU.

ACP rice directly imported into the EU benefits only from a 50 percent reduction in duty within an annual quota of 125,000 tonnes. Only 6,000 tonnes is expected to be imported within this quota in 1996/97.
